title: Access Control Panel Tamper and Line Fault
exclusions: Does not replace the manufacturer’s authoritative alarm console, certify wiring, or assess logical identity stores; badge-only denials without panel hardware faults, pure video analytics, or mantrap mechanical interlocks that never emit `access_control:panel` telemetry are out of scope unless translated into this sourcetype.
evidence: Export the saved search “Access panel tamper and line fault correlation” results (or the executive single-value panel) weekly to the physical security evidence share, retain the alert firing history table with `panel_id` and acknowledgement user, and snapshot the dashboard PNG for auditor walkthroughs.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=physical` sourcetype='access_control:panel' where `panel_id` satisfies detection threshold for UC-15.3.21 ('Access Control Panel Tamper and Line Fault'). Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `physical` / `access_control:panel` events where `panel_id` stays below detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `ops_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-15.3.21.

dataSources: Ingest controller diagnostics into `index=physical` as `sourcetype="access_control:panel"` with Splunk-extracted numeric flags **`tamper`**, **`line_fault`**, and enumerated **`power_state`**, plus dimensions **`panel_id`** and **`fault_type`** that your normalisation maps from the vendor feed. Land syslog or structured UDP/TCP from the access head-end through **Splunk Connect for Syslog** ([Splunkbase app **4740**](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/4740)) on a Heavy Forwarder, or forward compact JSON through **HTTP Event Collector** `POST /services/collector/event`, aligning timestamps and FIELDALIAS rules with the **Access panel diagnostics** normalisation app referenced for this stream.
spl:
index=physical sourcetype="access_control:panel"
| where tamper=1 OR line_fault=1 OR power_state!="normal"
| stats count by panel_id, fault_type
| sort -count
description: Supervised access-control field panels report enclosure tamper loops, RS-485 bus or cable-to-ground trouble, and loss of healthy DC power supervision; this use case surfaces those hardware-level fault codes before the door electronics can be bypassed or left unsupervised.
value: Supervised access-control field panels report enclosure tamper loops, RS-485 bus or cable-to-ground trouble.... Timely UC-15.3.21 alerting on 'Access Control Panel Tamper and Line Fault' reduces operational risk and delayed incident response before manual triage or audit channels escalate.
implementation: Schedule a high-severity alert when `tamper=1`, sustained `line_fault=1`, or `power_state` leaves the healthy baseline; page physical security and facilities, capture panel and door IDs for chain-of-custody, and mute only inside approved change windows that tag the affected `panel_id`.
visualization: Primary **splunk.table** of `panel_id`, `fault_type`, `power_state`, `count`, and last `_time`; companion **splunk.timeline** filtered to `tamper=1`; **splunk.singlevalue** for distinct compromised panels in the chosen window with drilldown to the underlying events in `index=physical`.
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
  by Authentication.user, Authentication.action, Authentication.src span=1h
| sort - count
dataModelAcceleration: Optional: if you FIELDALIAS panel actor context into the Authentication data model for reader correlation, accelerate only after cardinality review on sparse tamper volumes; most teams keep this search on raw `index=physical` with a fifteen-minute summary snapshot instead.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `physical`** — Planned work for 'Access Control Panel Tamper and Line Fault' shifts `count` over `span=1h` while `panel_id` remains in-scope for UC-15.3.21. Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `count` on `access_control:panel`** — Scheduled automation elevates `fault_type` without crossing configured threshold. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `panel_id`** — Health checks in `physical` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `access_control:panel`** — First 48h baseline for `panel_id` is unstable; window via `ops_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `panel_id`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
equipmentModels: RS-485 supervised access door panel (tamper and DC supervision)
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud search heads plus an ingestion tier approved by physical security; prefer **Splunk Connect for Syslog** (Splunkbase **4740**) or an equivalent Heavy Forwarder `inputs.conf` TCP/UDP listener, or route vendor JSON through HEC (`/services/collector/event`) with TLS and token rotation per docs/implementation-guide.md.
• Deploy or verify the **Access panel diagnostics** normalization package so events arrive as `sourcetype="access_control:panel"` on `index=physical` with `tamper`, `line_fault`, `power_state`, `panel_id`, and `fault_type` extracted in `props.conf` / transforms—spot-check `_raw` vs extracted fields in Search before alerting.
• RBAC: grant a `physical_security_analyst` role search rights on `index=physical`, `schedule_search`, and `edit_alert_actions` only for the service account that owns this correlation; map Splunk Cloud patterns to `sc_admin`-approved equivalents.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• Confirm the head-end exports tamper, RS-485 supervision, and DC feed alarms without aggregation delay beyond sixty seconds; document VLAN, syslog priority, and any passive TAP requirement in the facility runbook.
• Set retention hot/warm policies long enough to investigate tamper chains (commonly ninety days) while honoring privacy guidance on location fields.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
• Paste the packaged SPL (unchanged) into Save As Alert, set `dispatch.earliest_time=-5m` with `cron_schedule=*/5 * * * *`, throttle on `panel_id`, and require two consecutive fault buckets before paging line_fault-only noise.
• Add workflow actions linking to your access ticketing queue and on-site camera layout maps.

Step 3 — Validate
• Use a lab panel or maintenance sandbox to toggle the tamper switch under supervision and verify Splunk shows `tamper=1` with the correct `panel_id`; repeat with a controlled RS-485 disconnect if your vendor permits.
• Compare counts against the OEM head-end alarm console for the same fifteen-minute window.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
• Dashboard: table of `panel_id`, `fault_type`, last event; timeline of `tamper`; single-value for distinct panels breached in twenty-four hours.
• If storms or power transfer events correlate with mass `line_fault`, coordinate with facilities before muting; never silence `tamper=1` without human approval.
